title: Sparkline trip detector and transparent staged shedding
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and implement a low-latency "sparkline" trip detector and a transparent staged-shedding system that operates per-dependency, per-model, and per-tenant. The goal is to detect short-lived degradations quickly without overreacting to noise, and to shed traffic in graduated steps with safe fallback behaviors (cached responses, lightweight model variants, or routed regions). This ticket covers thresholding algorithm choices, interaction with existing SLOs, multi-region failover integration, observability, and an automated rollback policy.
background: Incidents in Q4-2025 and early 2026 showed repeated short-lived latency spikes on the serving runtime for several popular models. Global SLOs held over long windows, but user-facing latency and tail errors spiked for small cohorts (single tenant or model path) before conventional circuit breakers tripped. Existing per-tenant hard trip points either tripped too late or induced abrupt fallbacks that caused quality cliffs. We need a detector that responds to early signs and a shedding ladder that preserves quality and minimizes collateral damage.
plan: 1) Implement EWMA-based sparkline detector that tracks 50/95/99 latency quantiles and error-rate derivative over 30s windows. 2) Define fractional shedding policy: 5/25/60/100% steps with tenant-weight-aware prioritization. 3) Integrate with routing layer to prefer intra-region healthy variants, then cross-region fallbacks, then cached responses. 4) Add must-have guardrails: automatic re-evaluation window, minimum healthy-capacity floor, and a simulated dry-run mode. 5) Roll out to canary tenants in staging -> beta -> prod with metric-backed gates.
acceptance_criteria: Detector reduces mean time-to-safe-shed (MTSS) by >=40% on synthetic spike tests compared to baseline
Staged shedding must avoid >5% additional error-rate increase for unrelated tenants during experiments
Metric dashboards for sparkline events, per-tenant shed-rate, and fallback type (cache/variant/region) available in Console
Automated rollback triggers if overall global SLO breaches by >1% in a 1h window after rollout
Unit and integration tests for detector and staged-shedder; load test runbook and result artifacts linked
decisions: Use EWMA derivative-based detection (short memory) instead of fixed sliding-window percentiles to reduce detection lag
Adopt fractional shedding steps (5/25/60/100) so we can observe incremental impact and stop early
Per-tenant budgeted shedding: tenants with higher SLA/priority get larger protected quota before shedding
Fallback priority: 1) cheaper model quantized variant in-region, 2) cached prefix response, 3) cross-region equivalent model, 4) queued retry with client-facing 429 guidance
Safety net: never shed below a configurable minimum capacity floor (default 15%) to avoid total blackhole
comments: 2026-02-26 Maya Chen: Initial proposal drafted; flagged for reliability review. Linked a reproducer and spike harness in artifacts.
2026-03-02 Diego Rivera: Prototype detector implemented in runtime-proxy; simple EWMA works but noisy for very low-traffic tenants — added tenant-weight smoothing option.
2026-03-04 Priya Nair (SRE): Reviewed rollout plan. Requested explicit canary tenants and a dry-run mode that records but does not act for 48h before each progressive rollout.
2026-03-07 Liam O'Connor (PM): Agreed on fractional steps; requested telemetry labels expose 'shed_reason' and 'fallback_kind' for downstream billing/alerts.

2026-03-10 QA: Load tests run in us-west-2 staging: synthetic 3x traffic spike; detector triggered at median 18s vs baseline 32s; staged shedding limited error spread to 2.8%. Draft results uploaded to artifacts.
notes: Key trade-offs: faster detection increases false positives for low-volume tenants; we mitigate with tenant-weight smoothing and minimum floor. We intentionally prefer quality-preserving fallbacks first (cached/quantized) then region hop as last resort.
postmortem_plan: If this rollout causes an incident, run immediate rollback to previous breaker configuration, capture trace artifacts, run contingency runbook (re-route to dedicated capacity), and schedule a blameless postmortem with SRE, Runtime, and Product.
